Walk In Time ran well at Tipperary for second and, off a 2lb higher mark, she should have a say. Kalnoo managed to keep herself in the fight until close home over hurdles at Punchestown, so she should hold a place chance. My Friend The Wind bids to capitalise on a 13lb lower chase figure, but will need to bounce back from a non-completion at Limerick in April.

She ran very well on debut, finishing a staying-on fourth at Tipperary, and the eyecatching booking of Harry Swan really aides her cause. Elle Klassycco returns from over three years off the track with a hood and tongue-strap both reached for, which may dent some confidence. She ran very well on her second start, but the market shall inform what is expected after that long layoff. Beir Bua has shown ability so far and, out of a half-sister to Paisley Park, should be staying on.

He is just 3 lbs higher in the weights for that Kempton victory and comes into this contest on an unchanged mark from that effort last time out. Flatley was a winner at Wolverhampton back in March, and he is just 3 lb higher in the weights here; with a decent 2nd last time out on the turf at Chepstow, he can run well here and grab a place. Captain Corelli was in great form last season when landing the four-timer; if he can bounce back to anywhere near that form, then he will fill the places here.

selections.comment: AWAAFI was a very impressive winner on debut over 5 furlongs at Hamilton last time and probably went slightly under the radar that day due to Royal Ascot being on elsewhere. She was not particularly fancied in the market; however, she blitzed clear in the closing stages to win by just over 2 lengths in the end, always keeping on and winning comfortably. She will appreciate this step up in trip here, and although there is a penalty to carry here, she looks a useful sort who can go in again. The 2nd place horse, Aspiral, has since won in nice fashion at Carlisle; therefore, there is some substance to the debut form. Ruby's Angel was well fancied to win on debut at Newmarket; however, she could only manage 2nd that day. She was then again well fancied at Ascot but managed a 3rd place effort that day. She might have to settle for another place here, as she might bump into a nice sort. And Adalida is yet to finish in the first four in her career, and unfortunately she might have to settle for another place effort here.

She put in two game efforts at Kempton and Ascot for her last two runs of last season, and in both of those runs it looked as if this step up even further in trip would suit her. She doesn't do anything quickly but is a relentless galloper, and that could be put to good use in this contest. Pique has won over this trip previously, and although disappointing at Goodwood last time out, she takes a step down in class here, which could be more to her liking. Knights Affair has been mixing it up over obstacles recently, and although he might need further in the trip, he can still run well and fill the places here.

selections.comment: HEADMASTER has come second on both of his career runs so far and has already managed to scoop up almost 12k in prize money; therefore, that shows the level of race he has raced in already. A three-quarters of a length second on debut behind a horse with a run under his belt already, he was always keeping on well to the line that day. He then lined up as joint favourite at Windsor next time out, where he was just touched off by a neck in the end, getting beat by a horse with an extra race of experience compared to him. The step back down in the trip should be no issue, and this looks like a slightly easier task than his last two. Grey Jaguar is a half-brother to multiple Group 1 winner Mother Earth; therefore, he is pretty well bred. He ran well on debut over the extended 7 furlongs at this venue just a few weeks ago; he will run well here but might have to settle with coming 2nd once again. And Tokyo Joe ran well to come 2nd last time out; however, he is up against some nice types here, therefore he might have to settle with placing once again.

A repeat of that should be enough but there's likely a fair bit more to come and he can raise the bar considerably higher if pushed. Secret Force will need to find a fair bit to lay down a serious challenge to the selection but looks best placed to do so. He caught the eye on debut making late ground after being green early. He did a bit too much from the front last time, again over 1m2f, and may be suited to this drop back to a mile as long as he keeps tabs on the leaders early. Asian Journey is another who could get involved if building on his initial promise but Versailles Prince is more interesting and may just reward each way support

She can take the slight step up in grade in her stride and make all again. The unexposed top-weight Lady Of Andros is greatly feared having knocked on the door loudly the last twice and conditions look spot on for another big effort. A better effort from Raneenn looks likely. A couple of poor runs are off-putting but 7f here stretched her stamina last time and she was poorly drawn prior to that. A fast ground six furlongs looks ideal and she can bounce back and get a place on the podium. Arabian Leopard is interesting tried over 6f for the frist time and is a fair each way alternative

selections.comment: RENESMEE arrives in fine fettle having won last time out following three solid efforts prior to that this term and can show she's got the pace for a stiff seven furlongs. She's not tried the trip since early in 2024 but has been placed twice over it (seven runs) and looks worth chancing she can cope. If able to keep tabs early doors she can land this. Enpassant looks the biggest threat now he's found his level again and is capable of exploiting any shortcomings of the selection. The consistent Split Elevens shouldn't be too far away but third choice goes to Saved Lizzie. Her form seems to have dropped off a cliff the last three runs since a decent fourth in December. However, there have been possible excuses and if getting close to her 2024 form would be a threat. Her only try at 7f rates as a career best on the Flat and she could out-run her odds. Born A Rebel is also worthy of consideration as an each-way vehicle

Phantom Watch is next best, he made a promising debut at Newbury earlier this month and with improvement likely ought to be thereabouts. If there's one from the rest of the pack that could challenge the top 2 it would be Jungle Knight.

Havana Sky has been seen to best effect on AW after completing a 4-timer over the winter period, he was placed last time after a couple of below par efforts so could go well.
